Synopsis:
Altar dedicated to Shar. Has a ritual dagger on it. The altar appears when you activate three tapestries with dogmas of Shar.When the altar appears the door that leads outside gets locked. You need to recite the dogmas at the altar and spill your blood on it to open the door.If you a follower of shar you can do it with not issue and get a blessing.If you aren't a follower of shar, but you passed all the saving throws you can also get a blessing of shar by reciting the dogmas.If you didn't pass all the saving throws and perform a ritual then the guardians appear because you aren't worthy.If you desecrate the altar by taking the dagger then the guardians appear no matter who you are.

Cluster Contexts:
- TWN_CentralSquare_SharAltar.json: You’re in a hidden Shar shrine beneath the Central Square where an altar appears only after activating three tapestries that speak Shar’s dogmas; when the altar manifests the door out of the chamber locks. To open the door you must recite the dogmas at the altar and spill your blood on the ritual dagger; followers of Shar can perform the rite and receive a blessing automatically. Non‑followers can also gain the blessing if they pass the shrine’s saving throws, but failing those checks while attempting the ritual causes guardian spirits to spawn for being “unworthy.” Removing or otherwise desecrating the dagger (taking it) will summon the guardians regardless of your faith. Off‑screen the party has already been probing a Shar temple and allies like Shadowheart—who has personal ties to a Shar text—may have special dialogue or automatic success as a follower.
- TWN_CentralSquare_PlaqueOfWisdom.json: You’re in a hidden chamber beneath the Central Square confronting a Shar shrine that speaks the Lady of Loss’s dogma and asks if you accept her blessing. Saying yes triggers a check: success grants the shrine’s effect, failure inflicts a debuff and summons guardians to attack. If the player (or a companion like Shadowheart) is already a follower of Shar, a special dialogue option grants automatic success instead of risking the save. Off‑screen context: Shadowheart’s book about a nearby Shar temple and a mysterious “shadow curse” makes this shrine personally significant and may shape how she and the party respond.
- TWN_CentralSquare_PlaqueOfIntelligence.json: The scene is a secret chamber beneath Central Square centered on a Shar statue that offers a “test of your intellect” tied to Shar’s dogma. Off‑screen the party has been probing a Shar temple (and companions like Shadowheart have read a book about a Shar temple and a “shadow curse”), so allies may be personally invested or alarmed by the shrine. Accepting the test immediately produces a sensory effect (a faint purple aura and a pulse up the spine) and normally forces a saving throw — failure applies a debuff and summons guardian enemies; followers of Shar (or Shadowheart herself) have a special dialogue option that grants automatic success. The provided lines show the acceptance branch (player nods and the aura appears) but are only one possible outcome of the shrine interaction.
- TWN_CentralSquare_PlaqueOfCharisma.json: The scene is a hidden chamber beneath the Central Square (SCL_Main_A) dominated by a Shar statue with a plaque that asks whether you accept the Dark Lady’s dogma. In mechanical terms, accepting forces a saving throw — failure inflicts a debuff and spawns hostile forces — while a follower of Shar (e.g., Shadowheart) gets a special dialogue option that grants automatic success. Off‑screen the party has likely already been probing a Shar temple, fighting undead and agents of Shar (Balthazar and his minions are a possible example), so flags and tension around the place are already set. Shadowheart’s recent encounter with a book about a Shar temple and a “shadow curse” makes this monument personally meaningful, which explains her anxious/attentive reactions shown in the sample lines.
